title: Aureline M5 landing authorization
description: Canonical per-domain descriptor for the authorization that advances one reviewed landing candidate. Aureline only lands from an explicit reviewed landing candidate, never from ambient branch state, so this object names the landing path under authorization (a local squash plan, a local rebase plan, a merge-queue enqueue, or a review-ready export bundle), whether the truth is provider-authoritative or a local estimate, which actor is attempting to advance (an explicit user command, a background agent, or broad automation), and the resolved authorization state — including a protected-branch block, a stale-base invalidation, and queue-position ambiguity — so a protected branch stays blocked for background agents and broad automation unless the user explicitly advances the reviewed candidate through the correct command path. Names the object class, its change-orchestration association, the landing path, the authority source, the advancing actor, the protected-branch posture, the resolved authorization state, and whether a reviewed candidate is bound — so a land never begins from ambient branch state, a local estimate is never shown as provider-authoritative, and no member is silently reordered or retargeted. Downstream the landing-candidate sheet, patch-stack / queue, provider-landing, and support / export packets point at this schema instead of restating advance behavior by hand. Raw paths, raw provider payloads, secret values, and private endpoints never cross this boundary.
